source_book: Sri Chaitanya — FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students, Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition)
note: Question index for diffing and authoring. Stems restated in our own wording; the mathematics is exact. No solution content from the source book appears in this file, by policy.

questions.stem: Find the equation of locus of P, if the line segment joining (2, 3) and (−1, 5) subtends a right angle at P.
Find the locus of the third vertex of a right angled triangle, the ends of whose hypotenuse are (4, 0) and (0, 4).
questions.notes: Printed as ***i) under an unstarred question number 2; the two sub-parts are separate problems with separate solutions, so they are emitted as separate objects.

questions.stem: The ends of the hypotenuse of a right angled triangle are (0, 6) and (6, 0). Find the equation of locus of its third vertex.
Find the equation of locus of P, if the ratio of the distance from P to (5, −4) and (7, 6) is 2 : 3.
If the distances from P to the points (2, 3) and (2, −3) are in the ratio 2 : 3, find the equation of the locus of P.
questions.notes: Star prefix sits in the clipped spine gutter; three star glyphs readable, the first only partly.

questions.stem: A(5, 3) and B(3, −2) are two fixed points. Find the equation of locus of P, so that the area of triangle PAB is 9 sq. units.
A(2, 3) and B(−3, 4) are two given points. Find the equation of locus of P so that the area of △PAB is 8.5.
questions.notes: The book gives the area as the bare number 8.5, without the unit; sq. units is meant.

questions.stem: A(1, 2), B(2, −3) and C(−2, 3) are three points. A point P moves such that PA² + PB² = 2PC². Show that the equation to the locus of P is 7x − 7y + 4 = 0.
Find the equation of locus of a point P, if the distance of P from A(3, 0) is twice the distance of P from B(−3, 0).
Find the equation of locus of a point P such that the distance of P from the origin is twice the distance of P from A(1, 2).
Find the equation to the locus of the point which is at a distance of 5 units from (−2, 3) in the xy-plane.
questions.notes: Printed as *i) under an unstarred question number 10; the sub-parts are independent problems, emitted separately.

questions.stem: Find the equation of locus of the point which is equidistant from A(2, 0) and the y-axis.
Find the equation of the locus of a point P such that PA² + PB² = 2c², where A = (a, 0), B = (−a, 0) and 0 < |a| < |c|.
questions.notes: The question number sits in the clipped spine gutter on this page; no star prefix is visible, so 0 is recorded as the readable value and may be understated.
